adversarial: Re-run the golden chain with the BOM quantity doubled — expect SEAM_VIOLATION with stoppedAt null: every link green, the chain unsigned (a double-counted BOM can never sign).
Re-run with an unknown material — expect the chain stopped at parts-cad with the material named, later links never run, the receipt INCOMPLETE naming step + reason.

Re-run with an over-budget brief (bound 1 kg against 2 kg of parts) — links all compute, the mass-budget seam stands VIOLATED, the receipt unsigned. Malformed inputs answer NOT_COMPUTED missing_input naming the field (text / system.id / parts / integration).

Re-run the over-budget brief WITH fallback inputs declared — the fallback runs and its result lands in outputs.fallback, but the receipt still stands SEAM_VIOLATION, unsigned for the original request (a computed fallback can never launder an infeasible chain into a signature).
Declare fallback inputs on a FEASIBLE chain — expect the fallback SKIPPED with the reason 'chain feasible as requested — the declared fallback was not needed', and the receipt SIGNED as before.

notes: Fix of record: commit c33d86be7 on sx/core-loop (parent fa7d1f270; SX-CHAIN-RECEIPT landed alongside at fa7d1f270, its own check file) — orc.chain-run, the system chain over the landed wave-0 links as ONE run with named output-to-input mappings (chain definition docs/conkay/chains/system-chain.md · receipt spec docs/conkay/chains/chain-receipt.md · solver doc docs/conkay/solvers/orc.chain-run.md · tests server/tests/conkay-orc-chain-run.test.js). The one cross-link mapping beyond fan-out: mass-bom's budgetKg input IS the requirements link's mass bound — the brief's own number, carried by the chain. Two disciplines are the ticket's substance: (1) STOP RULE — a link returning NOT_COMPUTED stops the chain, the receipt stands INCOMPLETE naming step + reason, later links never run; a declared optional link that fails is a stop too. (2) THE FALLBACK IS DECLARATION-GATED (amended 2026-11-18) — F10 was ANSWERED by Ramaj first-hand (main chat 2026-11-18 ~06:44 ET), adopting the catalogue planner's recommendation entire: stated priorities govern when given, otherwise relax so as to minimize the largest relative change, the min-max version presented first plus up to two Pareto alternatives, every change citing the solver envelope that forced it, the answer shipping with its envelope worded 'closest within the stated envelope' (CB-0835 rule 2). SX-ORC-09 landed at f2ed241fb on sx/core-loop (head 3d4eac156): the permanent F10 skip is retired — the fallback step is OPTIONAL, runs when declared and the chain is infeasible (in place on a stopped link, after the seams on a violated seam, inserted before the report link), its result lands in outputs.fallback, and it NEVER signs the original request (SEAM_VIOLATION / INCOMPLETE stand); undeclared it stands SKIPPED 'not declared in the chain input (optional link)'; declared on a feasible chain SKIPPED 'chain feasible as requested — the declared fallback was not needed'; declared but NOT_COMPUTED, SKIPPED with that reason. Seams inside the signed artifact: mass-budget, part-mass-agreement (1e-9 kg per part), mass-total-agreement (two independent roll-ups), integration-verdict-carried.
